Initially, the patient was treated with levofloxacin and Unasyn for aspiration and community-acquired pneumonia . Coverage was broadened to vanco/Zosyn on hospital day 3 . After completing a week of antibiotics, she remained persistently febrile . She is currently being treated with multi-drug therapy for presumed pleural tuberculosis . Fever has improved since induction of TB therapy .

The patient presented with acute intracerebral hemorrhage of the right midbrain/pons/cerebral peduncle, likely due to hypertension . His blood pressure was initially controlled with a labetalol gtt, and anticoagulants were held . Repeat imaging showed the hemorrhage was stable . No other alternative therapies were indicated, and the patient refused a Factor VII trial . His blood pressure was eventually controlled on discharge with metoprolol, lisinopril, and HCTZ .

Acute renal failure likely started before presentation due to poor forward flow from initial cardiogenic failure and was probably exacerbated by 320 ccs of contrast received in the cath lab . She developed muddy brown casts on urine analysis . Due to hyperkalemia and anuria immediately post-catheterization, she was treated with CVVHD . She failed repeated trials off CRRT and is now likely dialysis-dependent .

The patient presented with abdominal pain and was found to have a necrotic uterus and abscess, requiring a subtotal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oopherectomy, and omentectomy . She developed sepsis with GNR/GPC bacteremia . Subsequently, she underwent another surgery for perforated diverticulitis with pelvic peritonitis, involving colon resection and colostomy placement . At discharge, the patient was stable, afebrile, tolerating a regular diet, and ambulating with assistance .

The patient's pain was well controlled with Percocet during the hospital stay . Discharge medications included Oxycodone-Acetaminophen 5-325 mg for pain, taken every 4-6 hours as needed . Acetaminophen 325 mg tablets were also prescribed, two tablets every 4-6 hours as needed . The patient was advised not to take the Oxycodone-Acetaminophen with Ativan .

The patient experienced bleeding from his gums and nose . This was associated with thrombocytopenia, with his platelet count dropping as low as 45K . Aminocaproic acid was used for gum bleeding . Reasons for low platelets include end-stage liver disease (ESLD), splenomegaly, critical illness, and antibiotics . The bleeding diathesis is related more to the platelet count than the INR .
